title: Should we list all config options and improve navigation?
description:
Some users have mentioned they wish they could change the `spark_install` location. This is already available with the `spark.install.dir` setting; however, this setting is under http://spark.rstudio.com/deployment.html which users wouldn't expect, I think.

Should we consider adding a `Settings` tab under `Reference` to list all configuration settings?

Should we also consider restructuring the navigation for the `sparklyr 0.6` release? Here are some the tab structure I would consider:

- Overview: Same as today's `Home`
- Guides: We could group here tabs for: Installation, Connection, dplyr, DBI, ML, Livy, etc?
- Deployment: We could create tabs for each deployment platform, as in: EC2, EMR, Cloudera, etc. rename `Deployment Examples` to `Guides`?
- Examples: Same as today.
- References: Same as today but would rename `Functions Reference` to `Functions`, add a `Settings` tab and rename `Additional Resources` to `Media`?

title: Need example to read from s3 bucket
description:
See: http://spark.rstudio.com/examples-emr.html

I don't we should move the "Download flights data", "Download data" and "Create Hive tables" sections to the end under "Advanced". Most users want to read from s3 buckets so we should rather include something like:

```{r}
config <- spark_config()
config[["sparklyr.defaultPackages"]] <- "com.amazonaws:aws-java-sdk-pom:1.10.34"

sc <- spark_connect(master = "yarn-client", config = config)
spark_read_csv("s3n://<path-to-data>")
```

See https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/issues/480

title: Use shinytest to do CI testing on the Shiny apps
braindump re: updates to sparklyr website
description:
## Global
- [x] Should we consider replacing all instances of Spark 1.6.1 with Spark 2.0.0, given that this is now the latest stable release?
## ML
- [x] Mention formula interface (currently does not accept interaction terms). We might even want to use it in preference to setting `response =` and `features =` in the examples.
- [x] Mention `ml.options` argument as an 'experts-only' interface for tweaks to Spark model output. In particular, `model.transform` as an R function that can be used to mutate the Spark model object before the fit is performed.
## Extensions
- [x] Mention the `ensure_*` family of functions, and that they should be used by extensions to enforce types for parameters passed to invoke (e.g. Spark routines that require an `integer` will not accept an R `numeric` element).
- [x] Mention `spark_compilation_spec` for users who would like to take more control over where the `scalac` compilers should be looked up.
- [x] Use actual blockquote styling for CRAN guidelines re: included Java code.
## Miscellaneous

I feel like we need to mention more of the `sdf_` functions as a more direct interface to Spark DataFrames that lies outside of the `dplyr` interface, but I'm not sure what such a section should be called / what it should live. Maybe a sub-section of the `dplyr` page?
